formats.label: Explanation and practice
useWhen: Explain an idea, compare alternatives, analyze evidence, or present a concrete case.
Give guided practice, a self-check, or feedback in prose.
avoidWhen: A paragraph merely describes what a future writer should teach.
A large block hides several distinct teaching steps.
requirements: Use plain instructional prose in value; Markdown is not rendered.
Split distinct ideas into editable blocks. An optional heading labels the block.

example.heading: Explanation
example.value: Explain the idea, connect it to a concrete case, and show the reasoning.

formats.label: Heading
useWhen: Separate meaningful parts of a lesson or introduce the concept inventory.
avoidWhen: The heading adds no structure or substitutes for an explanation.
requirements: Use title for the heading text.

formats.label: Concept definition
useWhen: Define one raw concept introduced in the lesson.
Review a concept already taught in the module.
avoidWhen: The card is a whole lesson, study advice, or a prose recap.
requirements: Use a concise title and definition in description.
End each lesson with a Concepts introduced heading and one card per introduced concept.
Summary cards preserve sourceSectionId when available and introduce no new material.

example.title: Named concept
example.description: A concise definition of this concept.

formats.label: Equation or formula
useWhen: Show a standalone formula, symbolic relationship, or aligned calculation lines.
avoidWhen: Words connected with mathematical symbols are being used as a metaphor rather than an actual relationship.
requirements: Use readable ASCII strings in equations; this is not a LaTeX renderer or calculation engine.
Explain symbols, assumptions, and units in surrounding prose or caption.

example.title: Relationship
example.caption: Use compatible units for speed and time.

formats.label: Worked problem
useWhen: Demonstrate a quantitative, formal, technical, or procedural task whose steps the learner can repeat.
avoidWhen: Interpretive humanities or social-science analysis, historical causation, literary interpretation, ethics discussion, or source analysis.
The example only restates a learning goal or forces a prose argument into fake equations.
requirements: State the problem, known information, target, reasoning steps, final answer, and check.
Keep equation lines as readable ASCII strings and verify calculations.

example.title: Worked problem
example.problem: Find distance traveled at a constant speed of 3 meters per second for 4 seconds.
example.check: Seconds cancel, leaving meters, and the result is positive.

formats.label: Image, diagram, or graph
useWhen: An available image helps learners inspect a spatial relationship, visual evidence, graph, or object.
avoidWhen: Only an imagined asset or unverified URL is available.
The image is decorative or carries essential instruction without a text alternative.
requirements: Use only a supplied or verified asset URL, with descriptive alt text and a useful caption.
Reference the actual supporting source and retain credit or license information where available.
Do not invent an image URL or embed SVG/HTML as a replacement block.

example.caption: Explain what the learner should notice.

formats.label: Video
useWhen: An available demonstration or animation makes a process easier to inspect.
avoidWhen: No supplied or verified embeddable video is available.
The video replaces the course's own explanation or practice.
requirements: Use a source-backed playable or embed URL; do not invent one.
Use integer clip.startSeconds and clip.endSeconds only when selecting a relevant excerpt.
Omit filler titles and retain the supporting source ID.

formats.label: Embedded resource
useWhen: A provided embeddable resource supports exploration or a procedure the learner must practice.
avoidWhen: No actual compatible resource URL is available.
The lesson would pretend to provide a native simulation, editor, or calculator that does not exist.
requirements: Use a supplied or verified embeddable URL and a descriptive title.
Explain the task in surrounding text and cite the resource.
Never substitute generated HTML or scripts for a resource URL.

formats.label: Quiz or test
useWhen: Collect question-based mastery evidence for taught material.
avoidWhen: Writing instruction or an ungraded practice prompt inside a Learn lesson.
requirements: Generate through the quiz assessment workflow in a separate Apply section.
Use question, options, and a zero-based answers array; obey the assessment plan's coverage and question-count requirements.

formats.label: Project or practical assessment
useWhen: Assess a project, analysis, lab, portfolio, or other submitted artifact against a rubric.
avoidWhen: The learner only needs a short, ungraded practice activity in a lesson.
requirements: Generate through the project assessment workflow in a separate Apply section.
Include instructions, required evidence, rubric criteria, a canonical submission type, and grading metadata.

example.title: Applied task
example.instructions: Create an artifact demonstrating the assigned outcome.
requiredEvidence: Artifact and explanation of the method.

criteria.title: Reasoning
criteria.description: The method is correct and justified.
